name: Von Willebrand Disease Type 2A

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: ISTH-SSC Diagnostic Criteria for VWD Type 2A

criteria.description: Demonstration of qualitative defect in von Willebrand factor function with decreased high molecular weight multimers
Personal or family history of mucocutaneous bleeding symptoms such as epistaxis, menorrhagia, or easy bruising
Reduced ristocetin cofactor activity to antigen ratio (<0.6) indicating qualitative VWF defect
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the VWF gene associated with type 2A phenotype
Normal or mildly decreased VWF antigen levels differentiating from type 1 VWD

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of bleeding history plus demonstration of qualitative VWF defect with decreased high molecular weight multimers and reduced ristocetin cofactor activity
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other VWD subtypes and acquired von Willebrand syndrome.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Mucocutaneous bleeding with prolonged bleeding time
searchTerms: bleeding from skin and mucous membranes with slow clotting
mucocutaneous bleeding with prolonged bleeding time
extended bleeding in mucous membranes and skin
bleeding lasts long after small cuts

common.symptomName: Postoperative bleeding disproportionate to surgical trauma

laboratory: Decreased high molecular weight VWF multimers on multimer analysis
Normal or mildly decreased VWF antigen levels
imaging: Imaging generally not diagnostic but may be used to evaluate bleeding complications such as hemarthrosis or intracranial hemorrhage
other: Family history of bleeding disorder consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Quantitative deficiency of VWF rather than qualitative defect
Reduced VWF antigen and activity proportionally
Deep tissue and joint bleeding more common than mucocutaneous bleeding
Occurs secondary to other conditions (e.g., lymphoproliferative disorders, cardiac defects)

redFlags: Severe mucocutaneous bleeding disproportionate to trauma
Recurrent spontaneous epistaxis requiring medical intervention
Family history of bleeding disorder with autosomal dominant pattern
references: Sadler JE. Von Willebrand disease type 2: a complex disorder. Blood. 1998;91(12):4397-4403.
Federici AB. Von Willebrand disease: clinical and laboratory aspects. Haemophilia. 2004;10 Suppl 4:30-37.
ISTH SSC Subcommittee on von Willebrand Factor. ISTH guidelines for the diagnosis of von Willebrand disease. J Thromb Haemost. 2014;12(2):312-324.
